title: Anaerobic respiration; Link reaction and Krebs cycle; Oxidative phosphorylation and chemiosmosis
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: RS02#t2 term and clue written for the game; RS02#t4 term and clue written for the game; RS02#t3 term and clue written for the game; RS02#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: RS02#N.3a, RS03a#N.3a, RS04#N.3a, RS02#N.5, RS03a#N.5a, RS04#N.11a, RS03a#N.7a, RS03a#N.10a.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Matrix
items.clue: The fluid enclosed by the inner mitochondrial membrane.

items.label: Outer membrane
items.clue: Smooth boundary layer that encloses the whole mitochondrion.

items.label: Intermembrane space
items.clue: Narrow gap between the outer and inner boundaries of a mitochondrion.

items.label: Cristae
items.clue: Folds of the inner mitochondrial membrane, holding the electron carriers.

questions.stem: What happens to pyruvate in the link reaction of aerobic cell respiration?

options.text: It enters the Krebs cycle directly, where it combines with oxaloacetate to form citrate.
It reacts with oxygen in the matrix, forming carbon dioxide and a two-carbon acetyl group that enters the cycle.
It is oxidised and decarboxylated to a 2C acetyl group, which coenzyme A carries to the Krebs cycle.
It is bound by coenzyme A, the enzyme that catalyses its conversion into citrate in the matrix.

questions.explanation: Pyruvate loses carbon dioxide (decarboxylation) and hydrogen (oxidation, reducing NAD). The acetyl group is bound to coenzyme A and transferred to the cycle.

questions.stem: How is the proton gradient across the inner mitochondrial membrane generated?

options.text: Energy released as electrons flow along the chain pumps protons from the matrix into the intermembrane space.
Protons are pumped from the intermembrane space into the matrix as electrons flow along the chain of carriers.
Hydrolysis of ATP supplies the energy needed to pump protons across the inner membrane into the intermembrane space.
Electrons themselves are pumped across the inner membrane, leaving the protons behind in the matrix.

questions.explanation: At each transfer from carrier to carrier, energy released is used to move protons out of the matrix, across the inner membrane.

questions.stem: During intense exercise, muscle cells convert pyruvate to lactate. What is the purpose of this conversion?

options.text: To release extra ATP from pyruvate once the mitochondria have stopped working.
To oxidise pyruvate so that more reduced NAD is available to the cell.
To convert pyruvate into a form able to enter the mitochondria.
To regenerate NAD so that glycolysis can continue producing ATP.

questions.explanation: Reducing pyruvate to lactate turns reduced NAD back to NAD. Glycolysis, which needs NAD, continues with a net two ATP per glucose.

questions.stem: One acetyl group enters the Krebs cycle and oxaloacetate is regenerated. Which account of one turn of the cycle is correct?

options.text: Two decarboxylations give off carbon dioxide, four dehydrogenations reduce carriers, one ATP forms.
Two carbon dioxide molecules form when oxygen oxidises the carbon atoms of the acetyl group directly.
Each of the four oxidations forms one ATP directly, so the cycle yields most of the cell's ATP supply.
Only decarboxylation occurs, since no oxygen enters the matrix to oxidise any of the cycle's intermediates.

questions.explanation: Per turn, two carbons leave as carbon dioxide, four oxidations by removal of hydrogen produce reduced carriers (mainly reduced NAD), and one ATP forms directly.

questions.stem: How does ATP synthase couple the proton gradient to the synthesis of ATP?

options.text: It hydrolyses ATP to pump protons across the inner membrane into the intermembrane space, building the gradient.
Protons flow through it down their gradient into the matrix, releasing energy that phosphorylates ADP.
Water moves through it by osmosis into the matrix, and the resulting pressure change forces phosphate onto ADP.
Protons collect in the intermembrane space and phosphorylate ADP there, on the outer surface of the enzyme.

questions.explanation: ATP synthase is the route by which protons diffuse back into the matrix. The energy released is coupled to joining phosphate to ADP: chemiosmosis.

questions.stem: Crucian carp can survive for months in ice-covered ponds with no oxygen. In these conditions their muscle cells convert pyruvate to ethanol and carbon dioxide, and the ethanol leaves through the gills. Which statement about this anaerobic respiration is correct?

options.text: It takes place inside the mitochondria, which is where the ethanol is made.
All its ATP comes from glycolysis: far less per glucose than aerobic respiration.
Converting pyruvate to ethanol releases extra ATP, which is why the fish survives.
It still uses the small amount of oxygen that remains dissolved in the pond water.

questions.stem: A student claims: 'Without oxygen the electron transport chain keeps running; only the formation of water stops.' Which statement correctly evaluates this claim?

options.text: Correct: the chain needs only reduced NAD to keep running, and oxygen is required just to make water.
Incorrect: the chain stops because the Krebs cycle needs oxygen to keep supplying it with reduced NAD.
Incorrect: with no terminal acceptor the final carrier remains reduced and electron flow stops.
Incorrect: the chain stops because without oxygen there is no ATP to power the proton pumps.

questions.stem: A chemical makes the inner mitochondrial membrane freely permeable to protons. Electron flow and oxygen consumption continue, but ATP synthesis stops. Which statement explains these observations?

options.text: Electrons leak through the membrane instead of reaching oxygen, so no energy arrives at ATP synthase.
Water enters the matrix by osmosis, diluting the ADP and phosphate so that they can no longer be joined together.
Reduced NAD cannot transfer energy directly to ADP, because the leak removes the protons that it needs.
Protons leak back into the matrix without passing through ATP synthase, so no gradient remains to drive ADP phosphorylation.
